note: Questions are typed exactly as written. points = one entry per fact the answer should contain; each entry lists accepted substrings (any one matches). Class 12 Physics needs Parts I and II ingested.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: What is combustion?
questions.answerShouldMention: A substance reacts with oxygen and gives off heat; the substance is called a fuel

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: What is pressure?
questions.answerShouldMention: Force per unit area

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: What is inertia?
questions.answerShouldMention: Objects tend to stay at rest or keep moving with the same velocity; the first law is the law of inertia

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Can you give me an example of it from daily life?
questions.answerShouldMention: Falling forward when a car brakes suddenly, falling back when a bus starts suddenly, or being thrown sideways on a sharp turn

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: What is diffusion?
questions.answerShouldMention: Particles of two kinds of matter intermix on their own; faster on heating

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: What is Ohm's law?
questions.answerShouldMention: V is directly proportional to I, provided the temperature stays the same; V/I is constant

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: So what happens if we double the voltage?
questions.answerShouldMention: The current doubles too, because V/I (the resistance) stays constant at the same temperature

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: What is corrosion?
questions.answerShouldMention: A metal attacked by moisture, acids etc.; black coating on silver, green on copper, rusting of iron

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What is Coulomb's law?
questions.answerShouldMention: Force between two point charges is proportional to the product of the charges and inversely proportional to the square of the distance; acts along the line joining them

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question: What is the photoelectric effect?
questions.answerShouldMention: Light of suitable frequency falling on a metal makes it emit electrons (photoelectrons); discovered by Hertz in 1887

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question: Why doesn't it happen with red light, even if the light is very bright?
questions.answerShouldMention: Below the threshold frequency there is no emission however intense the light; the threshold differs by metal; ultraviolet works on copper but green or red light does not

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: What causes lightning during a thunderstorm? Can you explain how it happens?
questions.answerShouldMention: Air currents move up and water droplets down, separating charges; positive charge collects at the top of the cloud, negative at the bottom; air stops resisting and charge discharges between clouds or cloud and earth

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: How do tiny microbes help my mother make curd and soft, fluffy bread?
questions.answerShouldMention: Lactobacillus turns milk into curd; yeast gives off carbon dioxide, and the gas bubbles make the dough rise

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Why do we hear an echo in a big hall or near a mountain, but not in a small room?
questions.answerShouldMention: The sound stays in the brain for about 0.1 s; the reflecting surface must be at least 17.2 m away

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.question: How does our eye manage to see both a far-away tree and the book in my hand clearly?
questions.answerShouldMention: Ciliary muscles relax (thin lens, longer focal length) for far objects and contract (thicker lens) for near ones; called accommodation

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: What is the difference between aerobic and anaerobic respiration, and which one gives more energy?
questions.answerShouldMention: Anaerobic happens without oxygen (yeast: ethanol and carbon dioxide); aerobic uses oxygen in the mitochondria (carbon dioxide and water); aerobic releases far more energy; muscles make lactic acid when short of oxygen

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: How does a transformer change a low voltage into a high voltage? Can you explain it simply?
questions.answerShouldMention: Works by mutual induction; primary and secondary coils on a soft-iron core; more turns on the secondary steps the voltage up while the current drops (220 V at 10 A becomes 440 V at 5 A)

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: Electricity (p.218) and Magnetic Effects of Electric Current (p.238)
questions.question: My mother always says never to plug the heater, the iron and the geyser into the same socket together, because the wires will get hot and the fuse will blow. I don't really understand this. Why does a big current make a wire heat up, and how exactly does a fuse protect our house?
questions.answerShouldMention: The heating effect of current (Joule heating); too many appliances on one socket is overloading; the fuse is in series and its wire melts when the current is too high, breaking the circuit

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Last week my little brother had a cold and fever, and the doctor said it was a virus, so antibiotics would not help. But when I had a throat infection, antibiotics made me better quickly. Why do antibiotics work for some illnesses and not for others? And how do the vaccines we get as babies protect us?
questions.answerShouldMention: Antibiotics kill or stop the growth of disease-causing microorganisms and are made from bacteria and fungi; they don't work on cold and flu, which viruses cause; a vaccine puts dead or weakened microbes into the body, which makes antibodies and remembers the microbe

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: My uncle says the internet comes to our city through thin glass fibres under the sea, carried as light. I thought light only travels in straight lines, so how can it go through a bent fibre without leaking out? And my aunt says diamonds sparkle for the same reason. Is that true?
questions.answerShouldMention: Total internal reflection when light goes from a denser to a rarer medium above the critical angle; a fibre's core has a higher refractive index than its cladding, so light reflects repeatedly and still travels when the fibre is bent; diamond's critical angle is very small (about 24.4 degrees), and cutting it well makes light reflect many times inside
